title: Trump says Iran ceasefire is ‘on life support’ as hopes for a deal fade
byline: US President Donald Trump said on Monday that a ceasefire with Iran was “on life support” after Tehran’s response to a US proposal to end the war made clear the two sides were still far apart on a number of issues.

title: Nearly 200 foreign nationals arrested over cybercrime activities in separate raids
byline: A total of 198 foreign nationals, including 173 Indians and 25 Nepalese nationals, have been arrested in separate raids conducted in the Galle, Hikkaduwa and Midigama areas for allegedly engaging in cybercrime activities, Sri Lanka Police said.

title: US says 18 passengers flown back after hantavirus outbreak on ship
byline: US Department of Health and Human Services officials said on Monday that 18 passengers from the luxury cruise ship hit by a hantavirus outbreak were flown back to the U.S. and quarantined, with the one passenger who tested positive in a Nebraska biocontainment unit.

title: Pressure grows on UK’s Starmer to quit as PM
byline: Britain’s Prime Minister Keir Starmer on Monday (May 11) vowed to prove his doubters wrong and stem mounting calls for him to step down after disastrous local and regional elections for his ruling Labour party.

title: Heavy rainfall above 100 mm expected in parts of the island
byline: The low pressure area located northeast of Sri Lanka continues to persist in the sea area vicinity of the island, the Department of Meteorology said.

title: Additional fertilizer relief announced for small-scale tea plantation owners
byline: Minister of Plantations and Community Infrastructure Samantha Vidyaratne, stated that the government has decided to provide an additional fertilizer subsidy to small-scale tea plantation owners.

title: Galle shooting victim succumbs to injuries
byline: The person injured in the shooting incident in the Dickson Junction area of Dangendara, Galle, has succumbed to his injuries.

title: One injured as shooting incident reported in Galle
byline: A shooting incident was reported this morning (12) in the Dickson Junction area of Dangendara, Galle.

title: Global fire outbreaks hit record high as ‘unprecedented’ heat extremes loom, scientists say
byline: Climate change has driven record-breaking outbreaks of fire in Africa, Asia and elsewhere this year, with conditions expected to get worse as the northern hemisphere’s summer approaches and El Nino weather patterns kick in, scientists warned on Tuesday.

title: Ex-President Mahinda Rajapaksa arrives at Bribery Commission
byline: Former President Mahinda Rajapaksa has appeared before the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) this morning (12) to provide a statement regarding the alleged SriLankan Airlines Airbus deal.

title: Schools closed in Deniyaya following flu outbreak to reopen tomorrow
byline: Schools in the Deniyaya Education Zone, which were temporarily closed due to a flu outbreak, are scheduled to reopen tomorrow (13).

title: US issues new sanctions over Iran’s oil shipments to China
byline: The U.S. government on Monday announced sanctions against three people and nine companies, including four based in Hong Kong and four in the United Arab Emirates, for aiding Iran’s shipment of oil to China. The ninth company is based in Oman.

title: ‘Fast & Furious’ TV series in the works for Peacock
byline: A television series based on the blockbuster “Fast & Furious” movie franchise is being developed for the Peacock streaming service, NBCUniversal said on Monday.

title: 16 major and 10 medium reservoirs spilling amid heavy rainfall across Sri Lanka
byline: A total of 16 major reservoirs and 10 medium-sized reservoirs managed by the Department of Irrigation are currently spilling due to the prevailing heavy rainfall across the country, according to Director of Irrigation (Water Management) Eng. H.M.P.S.D. Herath.

title: FM Vijitha Herath to undertake official visit to Belarus today
byline: Minister of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism Vijitha Herath is scheduled to undertake an official visit to Belarus from today (12) to 15 May 2026, on the invitation of the Foreign Minister of the Republic of Belarus, Maxim Ryzhenkov.

title: Man shot and attacked with sharp weapon inside home in Ambalantota
byline: A man was shot and attacked with a machete inside a residence in the Mamadala area within the Ambalantota Police Division last night, police said.

title: Mahinda Rajapaksa leaves Bribery Commission after recording statement
byline: Former President Mahinda Rajapaksa has left the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) a short while ago after recording a statement for over two hours.

title: Modi urges Indians to WFH and limit foreign travel as Iran war continues
byline: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has appealed to Indians to revive working from home, buy less gold and limit foreign travel to deal with a surge in global energy prices because of the continuing crisis in the Middle East.

title: TikTok launches £3.99 subscription for no ads in UK
byline: TikTok is introducing a subscription charge for UK users who do not want to see adverts on the platform.

title: 22 monks arrested with narcotics at BIA further remanded
byline: The group of 22 Buddhist monks recently arrested at the Katunayake Airport over the smuggling of “Kush” cannabis and “Hashish” from Thailand have been further remanded until May 26 by the Negombo Magistrate’s Court.

title: EU considering social media ‘delay’ for children
byline: The European Union should explore limiting children’s access to social media with possible new rules proposed within months, EU chief Ursula von der Leyen said on Tuesday (May 12).

title: Ex-Minister Piyankara Jayaratne leaves Bribery Commission
byline: Former Minister Piyankara Jayaratne left the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) after providing a statement regarding the controversial SriLankan Airlines Airbus deal.

title: Two remanded over alleged bail fraud in relation to Kapila Chandrasena’s case
byline: Two suspects accused of arranging two fake sureties to secure bail for former Chief Executive Officer Kapila Chandrasena, who recently died under mysterious circumstances, have been remanded until tomorrow (13).

title: Opposition writes to Chief Justice over President’s remarks on court verdicts
byline: The Opposition has submitted a memorandum to the Chief Justice requesting attention over a statement allegedly made by the President concerning a pending court ruling, according to its convener former Minister G. L. Peiris.

title: Dua Lipa sues Samsung for $15m over use of her image on TV boxes
byline: Pop star Dua Lipa has filed a $15m (£11m) lawsuit against Samsung, alleging it used her image on packaging for its televisions without permission.

title: Cabinet approves Rs. 112B govt-funded Rambukkana–Galagedara section of Central Expressway
byline: The Cabinet of Ministers has granted approval for the proposal for the construction of the Rambukkana-Galagedara section of the Central Expressway, with the project to be fully funded by the Government at an estimated cost of Rs.112 billion.

title: Now everyone equal before the law, President asserts
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake emphasised that both the political authority and public officials have a responsibility to ensure that the Rs. 500 billion allocated by the government in response to Cyclone Ditwah is utilised effectively and efficiently for the recovery and development of the affected communities and areas.

title: Cabinet subcommittee steps in to resolve land issues related to Uma Oya project
byline: A Cabinet subcommittee has stepped in to provide a permanent solution to long-standing land issues faced by residents in the Welimada, Uva Paranagama and Hali-Ela Divisional Secretariat areas, which arose due to the Uma Oya Development Project.

title: Dengue cases spike in Sri Lanka in 2026 – Health officials warn of further increase
byline: The number of dengue cases confirmed in the country has shown an increase compared to 2025, according to Community Medical Specialist Dr. Priscilla Samaraweera of the National Dengue Control Unit (NDCU).

title: Iran war has cost $29 billion so far, senior Pentagon official says
byline: The US war against Iran has cost $29 billion so far — an estimate that was higher than the $25 billion figure senior Pentagon officials provided to Congress two weeks ago.

title: Sri Lanka’s workers’ remittances exceed USD 3 billion in 2026
byline: Foreign remittances sent by Sri Lankan migrant workers reached USD 767.9 million in April 2026, marking a significant increase compared to the same period last year, according to the Sri Lanka Bureau of Foreign Employment ((SLBFE).

title: Advisory issued for severe lightning
byline: An ‘Amber’ advisory has been issued by the Department of Meteorology for severe lightning in the Western, Sabaragamuwa, North-Western and North-Central provinces, as well as in Trincomalee, Galle and Matara districts.

title: Landslide warnings issued to several areas extended
byline: Level 2 landslide warning has been issued to residents of Passara Divisional Secretariat Divisions (DSD) of the Badulla district owing to incessant rains experienced in parts of the island.

title: New Tamil Nadu CM Vijay thanks President Anura Kumara for well wishes
byline: Newly appointed Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu Joseph Vijay has thanked President Anura Kumara Dissanayake for his well wishes extended following the recent Assembly Election victory.

title: Top Labour minister Jess Phillips quits British government
byline: Jess Phillips has quit her role in Prime Minister Keir Starmer’s government saying she has not seen “the change I and the country expect”.

title: Uganda’s President sworn in for record seventh term
byline: Uganda’s President Yoweri Museveni, 81, has been sworn in for a record seventh consecutive term following his landslide victory in disputed elections in January, extending his tenure as one of Africa’s longest-serving rulers.

title: 12 spill gates of Rajanganaya Reservoir opened amid rising water levels
byline: A total of 12 spill gates of the Rajanganaya Reservoir have been opened as a precautionary measure due to prevailing adverse weather conditions and a rapid rise in water levels.

title: Public Security Minister signals possible closure of selected police stations
byline: The number of police stations currently operating in Sri Lanka has exceeded the required level, according to the Minister of Public Security and Parliamentary Affairs, Ananda Wijepala.

title: Court authorises technical assistance to access Kapila Chandrasena’s mobile phone
byline: The magisterial inquiry into the death of former SriLankan Airlines Chief Executive Officer Kapila Chandrasena was held today (12) before Colombo Fort Magistrate Pasan Amarasena.

title: Matt Damon and Ben Affleck sued by Miami cops over ‘The Rip’
byline: Two South Florida police officers claim Ben Affleck and Matt Damon’s recent action thriller “The Rip” used too many real-life details in its fictionalized narrative, causing harm to the officers’ personal and professional reputations, according to a defamation lawsuit.

title: Tourist arrivals in May top 46,000
byline: A total of 46,606 tourists have arrived in the country thus far in May, data from the Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority (SLTDA) shows.

title: Vijay urges Indian Govt. to secure release of arrested TN fishermen from Sri Lankan custody
byline: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay on Tuesday urged the India’s External Affairs Minister (EAM) S. Jaishankar to take immediate diplomatic steps to secure the release of six fishermen arrested by the Sri Lankan Navy and to retrieve their seized fishing boat.

title: Aravinda de Silva and wife testify in Kapila Chandrasena death inquiry
byline: Former Chief Executive Officer of SriLankan Airlines Kapila Chandrasena’s magisterial inquiry continued at the Colombo Fort Magistrate’s Court, where former cricketer and his relative Aravinda de Silva gave testimony regarding the events leading up to his death.

title: Sri Lanka, Pakistan discuss defence cooperation and regional security collaboration
byline: The High Commissioner of Pakistan to Sri Lanka, Major General Nayyar Naseer, HI (M), (Retd), has paid a courtesy call on the Deputy Minister of Defence, Major General Aruna Jayasekara (Retd), at the Deputy Minister’s Office in Colombo.

title: Several foreign nationals arrested over cybercrime network remanded
byline: The Galle Magistrate’s Court has remanded several foreign nationals arrested in connection with an alleged organised computer crime network.

title: President calls for expedited resettlement of displaced families in Kandy
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake has directed officials to fast-track resettlement efforts for families in the Kandy District displaced by the Cyclone Ditwah.

title: No sign of larger hantavirus outbreak, says UN health agency
byline: There is “no sign” of a larger hantavirus outbreak after the evacuation of the last passengers from a disease-stricken cruise ship, the head of the UN health agency has said.

title: Unawatuna massage therapist arrested over alleged assault on Australian tourist
byline: A 38-year-old employee of an Ayurveda massage centre in Unawatuna has been arrested by the Unawatuna Tourist Police over allegations of sexually assaulting an Australian woman, police said today (12).
